subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Dunning-Kruger Effect: Confidently Wrong
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Dunning-Kruger Effect: Confidently Wrong.

hook.text: A bank robber covered his face in lemon juice, believing it made him invisible to cameras. He was genuinely surprised.

buildup.text: Dunning & Kruger found that low-skill people vastly overestimate their ability.

discovery.text: The core problem: incompetence robs you of the ability to recognize incompetence — in yourself.

twist.text: As you learn more, confidence drops — the 'valley of despair.' Experts know how much they don't know.

climax.text: The most dangerous stage is knowing just enough to feel certain but not enough to see the gaps.

punchline.text: The less you know, the more certain you feel.

quiz.question: What did Dunning and Kruger discover?
options: Low-skill people vastly overestimate their competence

details.summary: The Dunning-Kruger effect shows that people with low competence in a domain tend to overestimate their ability, while experts tend to underestimate theirs. Ignorance breeds confidence because you do not know what you do not know.
details.whyItMatters: This effect explains why the loudest voice in the room is often the least informed, and why genuine experts speak carefully and with caveats.
takeaways: Low skill and high confidence often travel together
Experts underestimate because they see how much remains unknown
The cure is learning enough to see your own knowledge gaps

faq.question: Is the Dunning-Kruger effect just about stupid people being confident?
faq.answer: No. It affects everyone in domains where they lack expertise. A brilliant physicist may overestimate their skill in economics. The effect is about domain-specific metacognition, not general intelligence.

faq.question: How can you tell if you might be experiencing the Dunning-Kruger effect?
faq.answer: If you feel very confident about a topic you have only recently learned about, that is a warning sign. Seek feedback from acknowledged experts and ask what you might be missing.
